title: Boss: red team, blue team
summary: Estimate brute-force cost, write a constant-time comparison yourself, and stop a downgrade by authenticating the negotiation.

steps.title: Both sides of the table
steps.body: Three jobs that combine this module: an attacker's cost calculator, a defender's constant-time primitive, and a negotiation that an attacker in the middle can no longer downgrade without being caught.

steps.title: Brute-force calculator
prompt: Read lines of the form `<bits> <guessesPerSecond>` from standard input until the end (the rate may be written like `1e12`). For each, print:

where `<rate>` and `<years>` are formatted with `"E2"`, years is the **average** search time (`2^(bits-1) / rate`, 31,557,600 seconds per year), and the verdict is `broken` under 1 year, `weak` under 1,000,000 years, otherwise `safe`.
hints: `$"{years:E2}"` formats in scientific notation with two decimals.

steps.title: Constant time, by hand
prompt: Write `bool SafeEquals(byte[] a, byte[] b)` **without** `FixedTimeEquals` or `SequenceEqual`: return `false` at once if the lengths differ, otherwise look at every byte, accumulate `diff |= a[i] ^ b[i]`, and decide only after the loop. No `break` and no early `return` inside the loop.
The tests compare it against the library on many inputs.
template: foreach (var (x, y) in new[] { (dojoA, dojoA.ToArray()), (dojoA, dojoB), (dojoA, dojoB[..Math.Max(0, dojoLen - 1)]) })
Dojo.Eq($"agrees with FixedTimeEquals on {dojoRows} cases", 0, dojoBad);
Dojo.Check("two empty arrays are equal", SafeEquals(Array.Empty<byte>(), Array.Empty<byte>()), "said unequal");
hints: The only `return` before the loop is the length check.

steps.title: Authenticate the negotiation
prompt: An attacker in the middle can delete `TLS1.3` from the client's offer list, and the server, seeing only `TLS1.2`, happily picks it. Detect that the way TLS 1.3 does: the server authenticates **what it saw**.
Client and server share `key` (in TLS this comes from the handshake itself). Write:

- `string ServerHello(byte[] key, string[] offersSeen, string[] serverPreference)`: pick the first server-preferred option in `offersSeen`, then return `"<choice>|<tag>"`, where tag is lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 over the UTF-8 of `string.Join(",", offersSeen) + "|" + choice`.

- `bool ClientAccepts(byte[] key, string[] offersSent, string hello)`: recompute the tag over **the offers the client actually sent** and the choice in the hello, compare in fixed time, and also require that the choice is one the client offered.
If no option matches, `ServerHello` returns `"none|"` and the client must reject it.
starter: string ServerHello(byte[] key, string[] offersSeen, string[] serverPreference)
bool ClientAccepts(byte[] key, string[] offersSent, string hello)
solution: byte[] Transcript(byte[] key, string[] offers, string choice) =>
string ServerHello(byte[] key, string[] offersSeen, string[] serverPreference)
bool ClientAccepts(byte[] key, string[] offersSent, string hello)
template: Dojo.Check("the honest server picks TLS1.3", dojoHonest.StartsWith("TLS1.3|") && dojoHonest.Length == 7 + 64, dojoHonest);
Dojo.Check("the client accepts the honest hello", ClientAccepts(dojoKey, dojoSent, dojoHonest), "rejected an honest hello");
Dojo.Check("the server, fooled, picks TLS1.2", dojoStripped.StartsWith("TLS1.2|"), dojoStripped);
Dojo.Check("the client detects the stripped offer list", !ClientAccepts(dojoKey, dojoSent, dojoStripped), "accepted a downgrade");
Dojo.Check("an edited choice is rejected", !ClientAccepts(dojoKey, dojoSent, "TLS1.2" + dojoHonest[6..]), "accepted an edited choice");
Dojo.Check("a choice the client never offered is rejected", !ClientAccepts(dojoKey, new[] { "TLS1.3" }, ServerHello(dojoKey, new[] { "TLS1.3", "SSL3" }, new[] { "SSL3" })), "accepted SSL3");
Dojo.Eq("no common option gives none|", "none|", ServerHello(dojoKey, new[] { "SSL3" }, dojoServer));
Dojo.Check("the client rejects none|", !ClientAccepts(dojoKey, dojoSent, "none|"), "accepted none");
Dojo.Check("garbage is rejected without throwing", !ClientAccepts(dojoKey, dojoSent, "TLS1.3|zz"), "accepted garbage");
hints: Write one helper that computes the transcript tag from (offers, choice); both sides call it, with *their own* view of the offers.
Split the hello at the first `|`; the choice is before it, the hex tag after.
